parameter.help: The technical parameter that has to carry both opposing requirements: one measurable attribute of the system, for example wing length or hardness. Free text; an empty text clears the field.

requirementA.help: Requirement A — one side of the contradiction, together with its rationale (“should be A, in order to …”). Free text; an empty text clears the field.

requirementNotA.help: Requirement not-A — the opposite side of the contradiction, together with its rationale (“should be ¬A, in order to …”). Free text; an empty text clears the field.

problemNote.help: The problem note: why both requirements are impossible at the same time, plus background and boundary conditions. Free text; an empty text clears the note.

principleNotes.help: One note per separation principle: whether and how the principle applies to this contradiction. The four principles are time, space, condition and system (system level). The notes are written as a whole with all four principles; an empty text clears a note.

time.help: Note on separation in time: the parameter takes different values at different times, for example a wing that is extended for take-off and retracted in cruise. It records how this fits the problem.

space.help: Note on separation in space: the parameter takes different values at different places, for example a screw with a hard head and an elastic shaft. It records how this fits the problem.

condition.help: Note on separation by condition: the parameter takes different values depending on load, temperature or speed, for example photochromic glasses that are dark in sunlight and clear in shade. It records how this fits the problem.

system.help: Note on separation at the system level: the whole behaves differently from its parts, for example a bicycle chain that is flexible as a whole while its individual links are rigid. It records how this fits the problem.

selectedPrinciple.help: The chosen separation principle that resolves the contradiction: time, space, condition or system (system level); empty while none is chosen. In the interface via “Choose this direction” on one of the four cards. The solution note appears only after the choice. Any other value is rejected.

solutionNote.help: The solution note for the chosen separation principle: the concrete solution idea, what changes when, where, under which condition or at which level. It appears only once a principle is chosen and stays when the principle changes. Free text; an empty text clears the note.

swap.help: Swaps the two opposing requirements A and not-A against each other, in the interface via the button between the two fields.

params.command: The command as an empty object; it takes no arguments.
